subject: Promo credit issuance flagged — ACME Payments self-serve grant
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jul 2025 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: [ALERT] Promo credit auto-grant flagged: ACME Payments (acct acme-pay-3456)

Hi team,

Automated monitoring flagged a recent self-serve promo credit grant for ACME Payments (acct: acme-pay-3456). Summary of initial findings attached. Highlights: 3 signups that appear linked (same IP block + similar email patterns), two accounts used disposable domains, and the credit was auto-issued ($300).

I attached: signup-logs.csv (timestamps, IPs, email domains) and the account-profile.pdf. I recommend we pause token usage and decide whether to revoke credits pending manual review.

Questions for you:
- Do we block usage now or wait for manual confirmation?
- If we revoke credits, do we notify the customer proactively or after audit?

Thanks,

--
Monica Patel
Risk & Trust Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: signup-logs.csv (csv), account-profile.pdf (pdf)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jul 2025 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Promo credit auto-grant flagged: ACME Payments (acct acme-pay-3456)

Thanks Monica — looping in Neha for a quick triage.

My thinking: put a temporary hold on further token consumption and mark the credits as "under review" (do not bill the customer for rescinded tokens yet). If the pattern looks fraudulent, we should rescind and CC the customer operations note. If borderline, open a manual review with a short grace period and request company verification.

Neha — can you confirm the IP overlap and whether these emails are flagged in our disposable list? Also any previous interactions in HubSpot for this account (contact/POC)?

Date: Sun, 20 Jul 2025 12:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Promo credit auto-grant flagged: ACME Payments (acct acme-pay-3456)

Quick triage notes after reviewing logs:
- I see three signups in a 22-minute window (acct suffixes: -3456, -3457, -3458). All originated from IP range 198.51.100.0/24 (same ASN).
- Two email addresses use domains we classify as disposable (mailinator-like). The main visible contact (james.hollis@acme-pay.com) looks legitimate but was only added after initial signup.
- No HubSpot contact prior to these signups; the HubSpot ticket was auto-created this morning (linked).
- Risk score: medium-high (pattern consistent with promo-farm behavior).

Recommendation:
1) Immediately throttle token usage (limit to 10 rpm) and mark promo credits as "pending review" in billing UI.
2) Send a verification request to the listed contact (simple ask for company incorporation doc + a short note confirming intent).
3) If no response in 48 hours or docs fail to validate, revoke credits and suspend accounts.

I've attached a screenshot (suspicious-ip-screenshot.png) showing the IP cluster and timestamps. I'll prepare a short audit log for legal if we move to revoke.

-Neha

Attachments: suspicious-ip-screenshot.png
From: James Hollis <james.hollis@acme-pay.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Promo credit auto-grant flagged: ACME Payments (acct acme-pay-3456)

Hi Aditya / Neha / Monica,

Thanks for the heads up. I appreciate you checking in — ACME Payments is a real company and we started multiple trial seats for different product teams last week while we evaluate desktop vs server integrations. The second two signups were our internal dev contractors using personal machines to test the integration (sorry for the confusion).

I've attached a single link to our company incorporation PDF on Google Drive (https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-company-doc) and a short note from our Head of Engineering confirming the testing activity. Happy to hop on a quick call if you need more context.

Request: if possible, please leave the promo credits intact or grant a short extension — our onboarding schedule slipped and we'd like to finish a spike this week. If you require billing validation first, tell me what you need and we'll provide it.

Cheers,
James Hollis
Director of Integrations
ACME Payments
